cards.text: John, the servant God gave this vision to (Rev 1:1), just heard heaven roar that the marriage of the Lamb has come, and the bride was given "clothing of fine linen, bright and pure." (Rev 19:7-8). Then John looks up, and heaven is standing open. And there before him is a white horse, with a rider.

cards.question: The rider on the white horse has a name. What is He called?

cards.text: Faithful and True. The last name anybody stuck on me was a price sticker that said 25 cents, so friend, THAT is a name! And John says this rider does two things: He judges, and He wages war.

cards.question: The rider called Faithful and True judges and wages war. How does John say He does it?

cards.text: The rider has eyes like blazing fire and many royal crowns on His head, and friend, I wear ONE tall white hat and I still bump it on the oven hood. And there's a name written on Him.

cards.question: The name written on the rider is one that everyone around Him knows.

cards.text: Nope. Only He Himself knows that name. He's dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and John has another name for Him, one John CAN tell us.

cards.question: John says the rider's name is The Word of God.

cards.text: Then the armies of heaven ride out behind Him on white horses. Friend, I have never seen a parade like it, and I once watched six brand new cookie cutters line up for their very first batch.

cards.question: What are the armies of heaven following the rider dressed in?

cards.text: Fine linen, white and pure, just like the bride's. Now remember, His name is The Word of God, so watch what comes out of His mouth.

cards.question: Something proceeds from the rider's mouth to strike down the nations. What is it?

cards.text: A sharp sword. He will rule the nations with an iron scepter, and John says He treads a winepress, the kind you stomp, and this one is full of fury.

cards.question: The rider treads the winepress of the fury of someone's wrath. Whose wrath is it?

cards.text: One more name, and this one is written right on His robe and on His thigh. Me? I've got Dorin carved on my handle, and friend, most days you can't read it through the flour.

cards.question: The rider wears many royal crowns. What name is written on His robe and on His thigh?

answers.text: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS

cards.text: Then John sees an angel standing in the sun, crying out in a loud voice. Standing in the SUN, friend, and I break a sweat just opening my oven door.

cards.question: The angel standing in the sun cries out in a loud voice. Who is he calling?

cards.text: The birds. He tells them to come and gather together for the great supper of God, and friend, I heard SUPPER and grabbed my apron, but look at that guest list. That is NOT the supper I'm baking for.

cards.question: The angel tells the birds they will eat the flesh of kings, commanders and mighty men, and his list stops there.

cards.text: The list keeps going: horses and riders, everyone slave and free, small and great. Then John sees the beast, the one he saw rising out of the sea (Rev 13:1), and the kings of the earth with their armies, assembled to wage war against the One on the horse and His army.

cards.question: The beast and the kings of the earth line up their armies against the rider. What happens to the beast?

cards.text: Captured, and John doesn't even describe a fight. Friend, I've had longer battles with a jar lid, and the false prophet, the one who acted on the beast's behalf, gets captured right along with it.

cards.question: The false prophet acted on the beast's behalf. What did he do?

answers.text: Wrote new laws for the kings

cards.question: The beast and the false prophet are both thrown somewhere, alive. Where?

answers.text: The fiery lake of burning sulfur

cards.text: The fiery lake of burning sulfur. And the rest of them, the kings and their armies? Their end comes from the rider Himself.

cards.question: The rest of the beast's side are killed. What are they killed with?

answers.text: The sword from the rider's mouth

cards.text: The sword that proceeded from His mouth. And all those birds the angel called? They come, and they gorge themselves, just like the angel said.
